title: Auto-Hide Panel when triggered doesn't allow the cursor to interact with the app its hovering over without additional movement
line: Revealing an auto-hide panel with the pointer resting on a task icon now shows its tooltip without moving the pointer.
explanation: An auto-hide panel is a hidden layer-shell window that KWin shows again when the pointer pushes the screen edge. KWin only re-picks the window under the pointer on motion, stacking order, minimize and desktop changes, not when a window's hidden state changes, so a panel that slid in under a still pointer got no pointer enter and no hover until the next motion. The change makes input devices update their hover and focus whenever a window is hidden or shown.

commits.message:
input: update pointer focus when a window is shown or hidden

When an auto-hide panel slid in under a still pointer, the pointer focus
was not updated until the next motion event, so the panel got no hover and
no tooltips. Now input devices update their focus when hiding changes.

BUG: 518795

media.caption: Master: panel revealed with the pointer still on the Dolphin launcher, no tooltip after 3.5 s (top); a 1 px move shows it (bottom).
With the fix: same reveal, the tooltip appears while the pointer is still (top), and stays after a 1 px move (bottom).

review.text: Connecting `Window::hiddenChanged` (for existing windows and newly added ones via `Workspace::windowAdded`) to `InputDeviceHandler::update()` fixes the exact root cause in the right layer (KWin), ensuring pointer hover and focus are re-evaluated whenever an auto-hide panel or other hidden window appears or hides under a stationary pointer. Signal lifetimes are safe with `this` as receiver/context, `InputDeviceHandler::update()` already respects `focusUpdatesBlocked()`, and the fix is backed by both KWin autotests and consistent live verification.

reviews.text: Connecting `Window::hiddenChanged` (for existing windows and newly added ones via `Workspace::windowAdded`) to `InputDeviceHandler::update()` fixes the exact root cause in the right layer (KWin), ensuring pointer hover and focus are re-evaluated whenever an auto-hide panel or other hidden window appears or hides under a stationary pointer. Signal lifetimes are safe with `this` as receiver/context, `InputDeviceHandler::update()` already respects `focusUpdatesBlocked()`, and the fix is backed by both KWin autotests and consistent live verification.

Correct root cause in KWin: the auto-hide panel is revealed through LayerShellV1Window::setHidden(false) (via the deferred deactivateScreenEdge), and findToplevel() skips hidden windows, but InputDeviceHandler only re-picked hover/focus on motion, stacking, minimize and desktop changes. So a still pointer never entered the revealed panel. Connecting Window::hiddenChanged for existing and newly added windows mirrors the existing windowMinimizedChanged handling. Connections are tied to the window's lifetime and the extra update() is cheap and rare, so there is no lifetime hazard. Before/after evidence (3/3 no tooltip vs 5/5 tooltip while still) plus the hide, edge-glow and click-after-reveal checks support it, and the 2 PointerInput failures also fail on the base. Optional nit: a PointerInputTest case (hide/unhide a window under a still pointer) would make it easier for KWin reviewers.
